summary.text: Maxine Waters is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election in California's 43rd District. A former Head Start teacher and volunteer coordinator, she served in the California State Assembly from 1977 to 1991 and in the U.S. House since 1991, including as chair of the House Financial Services Committee from 2019 to 2022. Her official biography emphasizes her work on housing, financial services, health care and international debt relief.

paragraphs.text: Waters was born in St. Louis, Missouri, in 1938. According to her official biography, she was the fifth of 13 children raised by a single mother and began working at age 13 in factories and restaurants.

After moving to Los Angeles she worked in garment factories and at the telephone company, and attended California State University, Los Angeles, earning a bachelor's degree in sociology in 1970, according to Ballotpedia.
She began her public-service career as a teacher and volunteer coordinator in the Head Start program.

Waters served in the California State Assembly (District 48) from 1977 to 1991, rising to Democratic Caucus Chair. Her official biography cites state legislation on divestment of state pension funds from South Africa, a plant-closure law and a statewide child abuse prevention training program from that period.

She has served on the Democratic National Committee since 1980, according to her official biography, and was a leader in five presidential campaigns: Kennedy in 1980, Jackson in 1984 and 1988, and Clinton in 1992 and 1996.
She was elected to the U.S. House in 1990 and took office in 1991, representing California's 29th District (1991-1993), the 35th District (1993-2013) and the 43rd District (2013-present).

Waters became the first woman and first African American to chair the House Financial Services Committee, serving as chair from 2019 to 2022 and ranking member from 2023 to 2024; Ballotpedia lists her as a committee member in the 2025-2026 term.

According to her official biography, she founded Community Build after the 1992 Los Angeles civil unrest and Project Build in the 1980s, co-founded the Black Women's Forum, is a founding member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, and is a past chair of the Congressional Black Caucus.
The biography also states she is married to Sidney Williams, a former U.S. Ambassador to the Bahamas, and has two adult children and two grandchildren.
